title: Reliability Catalyst: Sprint Proposal & Initiative Brief
body:
Executive summary:

This note proposes a 6-sprint (2-week sprint) cadence to kick off the Reliability Catalyst initiative: a focused, cross-functional program to accelerate SLO adoption, reduce service-level regressions, and create repeatable onboarding artifacts for feature teams. The work pairs SREs, product engineers, platform, and customer-facing teams around short, measurable experiments (micro-bounties) aimed at (1) instrumenting gaps, (2) validating error-budget driven runbooks, and (3) closing observability contracts so feature teams can own SLOs with confidence.

Why this approach (high level):
- Current onboarding is ad-hoc: lots of manual guidance, little standardization across services.
- We need tangible wins to build momentum: short experiments with clear owners and measurable signals.
- Program must produce artifacts that scale (templates, test harnesses, automated checks).

Goals & measurable outcomes (by end of sprint 6):
- 10 services with production SLOs defined and wired to dashboards and alert rules (target: 10/10 smoke tests passing).
- Reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for SLO breaches by 35% for pilot services.
- Create 3 reusable artifacts: SLO definition template, observability contract checklist, automated SLO smoke test harness.
- Run at least 2 canary rollouts using error-budget gating policy.

Scope (in/out):
In: public-facing inference API routes, embedding pipelines, 2 internal infra services supporting routing and KV caching.
Out: on-prem/private deployment installs (separate program), billing/finance metrics, customer-specific SLO contracts.

Stakeholders & RACI (high level):
- Program Lead (Aisha K) — R: coordinate, remove blockers, reporting.
- SRE Champions (Liam O, Maya C) — A/R: operational design, runbooks, smoke tests.
- Product Owners (Diego A, Serena Park) — C: define user-impact windows, acceptance criteria.
- Platform Eng (Ritika S) — C/R: dashboards, infra changes, alert automation.
- Solutions/CS — I/C: customer impact mapping, feedback on runbooks.

Sprint-by-sprint outline (2-week sprints):
Sprint 0 (pre-sprint, 1 week) — prep & discovery:
- inventory services and current SLI sources (logs, traces, metrics).
- pick 10 pilot services and confirm owners.
- run quick gap analysis: missing metrics, lack of dashboards, no alert rules.
- deliverable: pilot roster + gap matrix.

Sprint 1 — Instrumentation sweep + SLO definitions:
- sweep for missing SLIs (latency p50/p95, error-rate, availability).
- standardize SLO wording and user-impact mapping for each service.
- create SLO definition drafts in Confluence (one per service).
- deliverable: SLO draft page + initial dashboard skeletons.

Sprint 2 — Alerting & runbooks:
- convert SLOs into alert rules and link to runbooks.
- create error-budget burn visualizations (short-term vs long-term).
- run tabletop for 3 services (simulate breach, runbook steps executed).
- deliverable: paired alert+runbook for pilot services.

Sprint 3 — Smoke test harness & automation:
- build an automated smoke test harness that validates SLOs by synthetic requests and compares against dashboards.
- integrate harness with CI for nightly runs.
- deliverable: smoke test pipeline + failure signal hooks.

Sprint 4 — Canary gating and routing policies:
- create canary rollout templates using error-budget gating (traffic ramp-down rules).
- test routing fallback policies between model variants / regions.
- deliverable: canary manifest + test run report.

Sprint 5 — Observability contracts & handoff playbook:
- finalize observability contract: required metrics, dashboards, alert severity matrix, ownership.
- produce handoff playbook and checklist for feature teams to adopt.
- run a live onboarding with one feature team end-to-end.
- deliverable: contract + onboarding playbook + training session recording.

Cross-cutting work (ongoing each sprint):
- weekly office hours for teams to get help (SREs + platform).
- triage board for instrumentation tickets (JIRA-RC-*).
- short writeups for every completed micro-bounty (internal blog + template).

Success criteria (how we’ll know this worked):
- Quantitative: 10 services have green smoke tests for 7 consecutive nights; average MTTA improvement >= 35%; 80% of pilot owners sign off on observability contract.
- Qualitative: feature teams report smoother handoffs, fewer post-release rollbacks due to missing monitoring.

Risk register & mitigations (top risks):
- Risk: Instrumentation gaps are larger than expected (missing traces, partial metrics).
  Mitigation: fallback to sampling + short-term proxy SLIs; escalate to infra for quick metric exports.
- Risk: Ownership friction (teams not prioritizing SLO work).
  Mitigation: micro-bounty incentives, executive sponsorship email + monthly leaderboard.
- Risk: Alert fatigue from naive rules.
  Mitigation: apply alert maturity checklist; only high-confidence alerts enabled initially; ramp severity.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Governance: who approves final SLO wording for public API (legal/comms involvement?) — decision needed by end of Sprint 1.
- Incentives: approval on micro-bounty dollar budget and recognition program.
- Tooling: confirm long-term SLO store (OpenSLO vs internal).

Meeting cadence / checkpoints:
- Weekly sync (30m) — program status, unblockers (mandatory for champions).
- Office hours (60m, twice weekly) — drop-in help.
- Sprint review + demo (60m) — every 2 weeks.
- Monthly review with Exec sponsor (30m) — metrics & escalations.

Artifacts to produce (minimum viable set):
- SLO definition template (machine and human readable).
- Observability contract checklist.
- Automated smoke test harness and nightly pipeline config.
- Runbook templates and tabletop scripts.
- Onboarding playbook + short training deck (10 slides).

Immediate to-dos (next 7 days):
- Confirm 10 pilot services and owners (Aisha) — due 2026-03-19.
- Create JIRA board and ticket templates for instrumentation bounties (Liam) — due 2026-03-18.
- Schedule kickoff and first office hours (Maya) — due 2026-03-17.

Notes to self / informal fragments:
- consider a "reliability bakeshop" weekly hands-on pairing session (1hr) where SREs pair with engineering squads on real instrumentation.
- find a quick wins list: 5 services with existing dashboards but missing error budget visuals.
- communicate clearly to product: this is "reduce user-visible regressions" not just infra hygiene.

Appendix: sample SLO wording (template)
- SLO: Availability of /v1/generate for paid-tier customers.
- SLI: successful HTTP 2xx responses measured by gateway logs, latency p95 < 3s.
- SLO target: 99.95% rolling 30d.
- Alert: page if 30m rolling burn > 50% of error budget OR 10m sustained p95 degradation > 2x baseline.

Appendix: quick links (working)
- Confluence: reliability-catalyst-background (draft)
- JIRA: JIRA-RC-212 (instrumentation sweep), JIRA-RC-213 (smoke-test pipeline)
- GH: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/tree/reliability-catalyst

End of brief.

(Feedback welcome — this is intentionally tactical; want to land visible wins quickly and then broaden.)
